The Avionics Laboratory previously had a Time Domain measurement system for obtaining the complex permittivity and permeability of materials, but it was limited to frequencies below 18 GHz.
The Frequency Domain measurement system described in the paper can obtain measurements from 12.6 to 18.0 GHz, overcoming the frequency limitations of the Time Domain system.
The theoretical analysis in the paper derives equations relating the scattering parameters S11(ω) and S21(ω) to the complex relative permittivity (εr*) and permeability (μr*) of the material sample.
Three main sample holder configurations were considered: open-air, coaxial airline, and waveguide-fed horn-reflector, with the horn-reflector system chosen as the best compromise.
The Ku frequency band from 12.4 to 18.0 GHz was selected for the Frequency Domain system, as the necessary equipment was already available in-house.
The overall accuracy of the Frequency Domain measurement system is claimed to be 5 to 10 percent.
The Frequency Domain system uses an accuracy enhancement modeling approach to try to reduce potential measurement errors from non-ideal components.
The automated Frequency Domain measurement process involves measuring the scattering parameters, applying the theoretical equations, and using custom control software.
Comparisons of the Frequency Domain and Time Domain measurement data showed generally good agreement for several sample materials.
The Frequency Domain system has the potential to make measurements at frequencies up through K-band (18.0 - 26.0 GHz) with the addition of appropriate waveguide transitions.
The rectangular sample holder design was chosen to closely approximate the theoretical infinite planar slab model, with concerns about higher-order mode effects.
The dual horn-reflector antenna configuration was selected to provide a near-uniform phase wavefront illumination of the material sample.
The Time Domain measurement system discussed in the paper used a 14 mm coaxial line, while the Frequency Domain system would use a smaller 3.5 mm coaxial line for higher frequency operation.
The Avionics Laboratory has been interested in absorber measurements since the early 1970s and is aware of the challenges involved.
The Frequency Domain measurement system was developed under Work Unit 76331309 at the Avionics Laboratory.
